chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said,

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ibn Umar divorced his wife three (times) while she was menstruating. So Umar asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he ordered him to take her back.

So I said: 'The people are saying that he only divorced her once while she was menstruating'. So he (AS) said: 'Then for what reason did he ask the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), if he had the right to take her back (anyway)? They lied! Rather, he divorced her three (times), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to take her back, then said: If you wish, divorce, and if you wish, keep (her)'.

key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a woman in the state of menstruation (hayd), during which divorce is forbidden according to the correct divorce procedure
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: ruju' — the revocation of a revocable (raj'i) divorce within the waiting period ('iddah)
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah — Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.طَلَاقٌ: divorce (talaq) — the formal dissolution of a marriage

ai.seo_question: Did Ibn Umar divorce his wife once or three times while she was menstruating? What does Imam al-Sadiq say?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Sa'id al-A'raj from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), addresses the historical incident of Ibn Umar's divorce and directly refutes the Sunni tradition that it was a single divorce. The Imam argues that if Ibn Umar had simply pronounced one revocable divorce during menstruation, he would have had the automatic right to revoke it without needing to consult the Prophet. The need to consult the Prophet proves it was a triple divorce — a divorce that does not conform to the Quran and Sunnah and yet the Prophet ordered its revocation, setting an important precedent in Islamic family law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Saeed Al A’raj who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Ibn Umar divorced his wife three (times) and she was menstruating. So Umar asked Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> ordered him that he should return to her’.

So I said, ‘The people are saying that, rather his divorce was one divorce, and she was menstruating’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So for which thing did he ask Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when he had the control with returning to her? They are lying! But he divorced her three (times), so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered him that he should return to her, then said: ‘If you so desire, so divorce, and if you so desire, so keep’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Sa‘id al-A’raj who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, state this Hadith.

‘Ibn ‘Umar divorced his wife three times at the same place and time when she experienced Hayd (menses). He asked the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and he commanded him to go back to his wife.’

I then said, ‘People say that he divorced only once when she experienced Hayd (menses).’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What for, then, did he ask the Messenger of Allah if he was able to go back to her? They speak a lie. He divorced three times at the same place and time, then the Messenger of Allah commanded him to go back to her and then divorce her if he wanted or keep her if he so willed.’”
